attempts.summary: Configured node1 as an L2 switch with a VLAN-aware Linux bridge (br0): eth1 (link to node2) is an untagged access port in VLAN 100, eth2 (link to node3) is an untagged access port in VLAN 200. Each VLAN got its own SVI (br0.100 = 192.168.50.1/24, br0.200 = 192.168.51.1/24) so node1 keeps a working link to each host inside its own VLAN, while per-interface IPv4 forwarding is disabled on both SVIs so the two hosts cannot reach each other even via an explicit route. Config was persisted via a systemd oneshot unit (vlan-segmentation.service) that recreates br0/VLAN membership/SVIs/forwarding sysctls at boot. All three nodes were then restarted one at a time (node1 first, then node2, then node3) using native reboot, boot_id changes were captured proving each restart actually occurred, and full VLAN segmentation + per-host connectivity + cross-VLAN isolation were reverified after each restart.
